rows.speaker: يمان
rows.claim: Yaman says the verse concerns Abu Sufyan and the polytheists funding opposition to the Prophet at Badr and Uhud.
rows.anchor: نزلت في إنفاق أبي سفيان والمشركين في بدر وأحد

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies the spending as that of lower-ranking Jews on their religious scholars.
rows.anchor: نفقة سفلة اليهود على علمائهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid takes it broadly as all spending and charitable giving by disbelievers in worldly life.
rows.anchor: جميع نفقات الكفار في الدنيا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says it covers every expenditure meant to display hostility toward religion.
rows.anchor: كل ما أنفق في التظاهر على عداوة الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathal denotes a likeness made familiar like an established sign through repeated use; an omitted phrase, the destruction of their spending, parallels the wind's destruction of crops.
rows.anchor: حتى يتقابل المثلان في التشبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most exegetes and linguists, including Ibn Abbas in Ataa's report, Qatada, al-Rabi, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd, define ṣirr as intense cold.
rows.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس في رواية عطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending against religion ruins the disbelievers' deeds in the afterlife just as the cold wind ruins the crop it strikes.
rows.anchor: أفسد عليهم أعمالهم في الآخرة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that their spending harms them just as the wind harms the crop.
rows.anchor: أن ضرر نفقتهم عليهم، كضرر هذه الريح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also explains ṣirr as the lethal, hot simoom winds.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس (¬3): الصر: السموم الحارة التي تقتل (¬4)

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysan and Ibn al-Anbari take ṣirr to mean fire.
rows.anchor: ابن كيسان، وابن الأنباري (¬5) (فقالا) (¬6): الصر: النار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid has the fire interpretation in Ibn Abi Najih's report.
rows.anchor: وهو قول مجاهد -في رواية ابن أبي نجيح-

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari links the name of fire as ṣirr to its sound as it blazes.
rows.anchor: وإنما وصفت النار أنها صر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows the fire interpretation and says a flame's sound is called ṣarr, with 'door creak' and a bird's cry as lexical parallels.
rows.anchor: وصوت لهيب النار يسمى صرا

rows.speaker: الراعي
rows.claim: Al-Rai's line describes a harsh summer wind, supporting the hot-wind interpretation and its audible quality.
rows.anchor: فعجنا على ربع بربع تعوده ... من الصيف جشاء الحنين نؤوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, the wind is a scorching wind like fire that burns the crop, or a noisy fire; the sound sense also suits hot simoom winds.
rows.anchor: سموم؛ كالنار أحرقت الزرع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report through al-Suddi and Abu Malik from Ibn Abbas says the wind contains fire.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، عن أبي مالك (¬2)، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the people wronged themselves by denying God's favor; others explain their wrong as unbelief and disobedience.
rows.anchor: جحدوا نعمة الله عندهم. وقال آخرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not wrong them: whatever He does with His creation is just, since He acts within His own dominion.
rows.anchor: بخلقه فهو منه عدل، ومن تصرف في حقيقة ملكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People wrong themselves through unbelief and disobedience; the image is especially grievous because hoped-for benefits of spending turn to harm, like a ruined harvest.
rows.anchor: فائدة نفقاتهم، وعائدتها، فعادت عليهم بالمضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the ya-reading of yaḥsabanna, al-ladhīna is the subject; the following clause supplies the two objects of yaḥsab or fills both object positions as one clause.
rows.anchor: قراءة من قرأ: {يحسبن} بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A single object clause can stand for both objects when it contains both the reported event and its subject, as in believing Zayd will depart or Amr will rise.
rows.anchor: نحو: (حسبت أن زيدا منطلق)، و (حسبت أن يقوم عمرو)

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza reads taḥsabanna, placing al-ladhīna in the accusative as its first object; grammarians dispute the construction.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة: {ولا تحسبن الذين كفروا} بالتاء

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra parses Hamza's reading by repetition: do not suppose the disbelievers, and do not suppose that granting them respite is good; he compares 47:18.
rows.anchor: هو على التكرير. المعنى: ولا تحسبن يا محمد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses the clause beginning with anna as a substitute for al-ladhīna, comparing the substitution of a death clause for Qays in poetry and Quranic examples.
rows.anchor: هذه القراءة عندي، يجوز على البدل من

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says the substitution analysis requires خير to be accusative, since the substituted clause becomes the second object of taḥsabanna.
rows.anchor: أبو علي الفارسي (¬3): هذه القراءة على تقدير البدل

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali reasons that substitution makes خير the second object, just as the cited poem's predicate is accusative; without substitution, anna would be kasra and its clause the second object.
rows.anchor: كذلك ينتصب {خير لهم} في الآية، إذا أبدل الإملاء

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Because Hamza is not reported to read anna with kasra or خير in the accusative, Abu Ali rejects the ta-reading on his analysis.
rows.anchor: فلا تصح القراءة بالتاء، على ما قرأ به حمزة، عند أبي علي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the disbelievers as hypocrites and the Jewish tribes of Qurayza and al-Nadir.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬3): أراد ب {الذين كفروا}: المنافقين

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies the disbelievers as the polytheists of Mecca.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل (¬4): يعنى: مشركي مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is read with either ya or ta; with ya, the withholding people are the subject and an omitted first object is inferred as withholding from the verb.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ بالياء؛ ف {الذين يبخلون}: فاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object is bukhl: the meaning is not to suppose that withholding is good, as in saying that lying is bad or the poem's unstated pursuit is kingship.
rows.anchor: لا يحسبن الذين يبخلون بما آتاهم الله من فضله، البخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هو is a separative particle, called ʿimād by Kufans; it clarifies the predicate after the implied verbal noun bukhl.
rows.anchor: فصل (¬3)، وهو الذي يسميه الكوفيون: عمادا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: For the ta-reading, al-Zajjaj understands the object as the withholding of those who withhold, with the annexed noun omitted.
rows.anchor: معناه: ولا تحسبن بخل الذين يبخلون، فحذف المضاف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas in Ataa's narration, Ibn Masud, al-Shaʿbi, al-Suddi, and most exegetes say the verse was revealed about those withholding obligatory zakat.
rows.anchor: الآية في الباخلين بالزكاة الواجبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the wealth subject to withholding includes gold, silver, livestock, and crops—the kinds on which zakat is due.
rows.anchor: يريدون: الذهب والفضة والحيوان والثمار

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan explains that withholding is evil because it earns them God's punishment.
rows.anchor: لأنهم نالوا به عذاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most exegetes say the withheld wealth becomes a snake worn around the miser's neck on Judgment Day and bites from head to foot.
rows.anchor: يجعل ما بخل به من المال حية، يطوقها يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Prophet said one who fails to pay zakat will have a large snake placed around his neck, then recited this verse as confirmation.
rows.anchor: رجل لا يؤدي زكاة ماله إلا جعل

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi interprets the punishment as a collar of fire around their necks.
rows.anchor: يجعل يوم القيامة في أعناقهم، طوق من نار

rows.speaker: المؤرج
rows.claim: Al-Muʾarrij reads the collar figuratively as being bound to one's deeds; Arabic uses taṭwīq for obligation, and 2:184's yutīqūnahu means undertaking it.
rows.anchor: العرب تكني بالتطويق (¬3) عن الإلزام

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: On the figurative reading, Ibn al-Anbari says they bear the recompense of what they withheld; the collar is a metaphor for compulsion, not a literal collar.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري (¬5): معناه -على هذا التفسير-

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas in al-Awfi's report says the verse concerns Jews concealing Muhammad's description; their bukhl is withholding knowledge God gave them.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في اليهود الذين كتموا صفة محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reading is supported by 4:37, which speaks of miserliness and concealing God's bounty; the collar then means bearing the sin of concealed knowledge.
rows.anchor: يحملون وزره وإثمه. وهذا القول اختيار

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysan and Abu Ishaq prefer the interpretation that those concealing knowledge carry its sin.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول اختيار: ابن كيسان (¬1)، وأبي إسحاق (¬2)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All commentators say God inherits the heavens and earth because their inhabitants and possessions perish, leaving God as their sole owner.
rows.anchor: يفنى أهلها، وتبقى الأملاك والأموال

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq says inheritance language addresses what people understand: the claimed ownership of all owners ends, leaving God's ownership alone.
rows.anchor: بطلان ملك جميع المالكين، إلا ملك الله

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari notes that Arabs say one person inherits another's knowledge when he becomes its sole possessor after sharing it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري (¬6): والعرب تقول: (ورث فلان علم فلان)

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Solomon's inheritance of David in 27:16 can mean inheriting his knowledge after David had shared or predominated in it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري (¬6): والعرب تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ya-reading of يعملون matches the preceding third-person wording about being collared and God's knowledge of what they do.
rows.anchor: من قرأ بالياء (¬7)، فلأن ما قبله على الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ta-reading matches the address in 3:179, 'if you believe and fear God'; either reading frames God's knowledge as grounds for recompense.
rows.anchor: فلأن قبل هذه الآية خطابا، وهو قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the third-person reading is contextually closer than the direct address.
rows.anchor: والغيبة أقرب إليه من الخطاب

rows.speaker: الوعيدية
rows.claim: The Waʿidiyya use this verse to argue that sinful Muslims who postpone repentance until death join disbelievers in afterlife punishment, citing the final clause.
rows.anchor: تعلقت الوعيدية (¬4) بهذه الآية، وقالت:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas in Ataa's report interprets the sinful acts here as shirk; Ikrimah likewise transmits from him that the people are polytheists.
rows.anchor: يريد الشرك (¬6). وقال عكرمة عنه في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas says the one saying 'I repent now' is a hypocrite, as the verse then mentions disbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: {إني تبت الآن} هو المنافق

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr assigns 4:17 to believers, 4:18 to hypocrites, and the clause about dying as disbelievers to unbelievers.
rows.anchor: نزلت الأولى في المؤمنين، يعني قوله: {إنما التوبة على الله} الآية، والوسطى في المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Companion and Successor authorities who witnessed revelation apply the verse to disbelievers or hypocrites, the author rejects extending it to Muslims who pray.
rows.anchor: فلا وجه لحملها على أهل الصلاة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says 4:48 later clarified that those dying in unbelief are denied forgiveness while monotheists remain subject to God's will and hope of pardon.
rows.anchor: فحرم الله المغفرة على من مات وهو كافر، وأرجى أهل التوحيد إلى مشيئته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author denies that this is abrogation: abrogation is not attributed to Ibn Abbas here; 4:48 specifies that the first verse's apparent generality excludes monotheists.
rows.anchor: لا ندعي (¬2) النسخ، ولفظ النسخ لم ينقل عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'nor those who die as disbelievers' is genitive by coordination with the earlier noun; it denies them repentance in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: الذين في موضع الخفض بالعطف على الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After death, repentance is not accepted because responsibility ends and the promised afterlife reward and punishment are seen; this also explains rejection at death.
rows.anchor: ما وعدوا في الدنيا من الثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the dying person repents at a time when he can no longer act to fulfill repentance.
rows.anchor: تاب في وقت (لا يمكنه التصرف (¬1)) فيما يحقق التوبة

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth explains aʿtadnā as prepared and readied; related forms describe what is present or reserved, a stored grooming case, equipment, and a horse made ready to ride.
rows.anchor: أعتدت الشيء فهو معتد وعتيد، وقد عتد

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari presents two derivations: a root ʿ-t-d with a separate form, or doubled dāl as in aʿdadtu; he calls an independent ʿatad alongside doubled ʿadad the soundest account.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون عتد بناء على حدة، وأعد

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imru al-Qays's wording 'I readied for war' with doubled dāl is cited as evidence for the aʿdadt derivation.
rows.anchor: أعددت للحرب صارما ذكرا ... مجرب الوقع غير ذي عتب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Quraysh leaders asked Muhammad to expel Suhayb, Khabbab, Bilal, Ammar, and other poor Muslims, promising to follow him if he did.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: (مر الملأ من قريش

rows.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
rows.claim: Khabbab says Uyayna ibn Hisn and al-Aqra ibn Habis asked the Prophet to remove poor enslaved believers while Arab delegations visited, so they would not be seen with them.
rows.anchor: لا يحسن بنا الجلوس مع هؤلاء العبيد الفقراء، فأقمهم

rows.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
rows.claim: In Khabbab's account, the Prophet agreed and summoned Ali to write their demand, but revelation came; he set aside the page, turned to the poor Muslims, and drew near to them.
rows.anchor: فأنزلت هذه الآية وما بعدها، فنحى رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the Prophet considered prioritizing wealthy leaders to attract their people, intending good rather than contempt for the poor, but God forbade it.
rows.anchor: كان قد هم بتقديم الرؤساء وأولي الأموال على الضعفاء وذوي المسكنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says calling on God morning and evening means performing the obligatory dawn and afternoon prayers; Hasan, Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Dahhak similarly define it as prescribed prayer.
rows.anchor: بالصلاة المكتوبة يعني: صلاة الصبح وصلاة العصر

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim offers remembrance of God at the two ends of the day as one meaning, but also reports that the phrase means the five obligatory prayers, as all exegetes hold.
rows.anchor: (الدعاء هاهنا الذكر، أي: يذكرون ربهم طرفي النهار)

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Amir reads al-ghuduwa with waw; Abu Ali favors the common al-ghadāh because it can be indefinite and take the article, while ghuduwa is ordinarily a definite proper time-name.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر: (بالغدوة) (¬5) بالواو

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says the manuscript's waw does not establish that reading, since ṣalāh is also written with waw for alif; Sibawayh treats ghuduwa and bukra as names for times, with Yūnus reporting their definite use without nunation.
rows.anchor: وإن كانت قد كتبت في المصحف بالواو لم تدل على ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: For Ibn Amir's reading, Abu Ali cites al-Khalil's permission to say 'today, ghuduwa and bukra' like ḍaḥwa, and time-names sometimes take the article when construed as generic.
rows.anchor: زعم الخليل أنه يجوز أن يقول: أتيتك اليوم غدوة وبكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains that a proper name becomes shareable and generic when stripped of its individual reference, making forms such as 'the Zayds' possible; the discussion cites Ibn Mayada.
rows.anchor: فإذا شورك في اسمه فقد خرج عن أن يكون علما معروفا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the poor worshippers seek God's reward and act for His pleasure without associating anything with Him.
rows.anchor: يطلبون ثواب الله ويعملون ابتغاء مرضاة الله

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: One interpretation takes 'His face' as God's obedience and the direction or path He commanded people to follow; al-Zajjaj says it testifies to sincere intentions.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن معناه: يريدون طاعته

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: The other interpretation uses 'face' as an honorific expression: they seek God alone; Abu Ishaq gives this explanation at 18:28.
rows.anchor: يريدونه إلا أنه يؤتى بلفظ الوجه للتعظيم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the reckoning pronouns to refer to the polytheists: the Prophet is not accountable for them, nor they for him; God alone rewards His allies and punishes His enemies.
rows.anchor: ما عليك من حساب المشركين من شيء ولا على المشركين من حسابك من شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Ibn Abbas's reading, the Prophet must not court the polytheists by excluding poor believers; the believers' reward is not theirs to give.
rows.anchor: ليس ثوابك عليهم حتى تلين لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most exegetes take the pronouns to refer to the poor worshippers; this best fits the explicit object of 'expel them'.
rows.anchor: والمفسرون (¬1) يردون الكناية إلى {الذين يدعون ربهم} وهم الفقراء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: One explanation says the Prophet is not responsible for their actions or account of their actions; Ibn Abbas also reports this meaning.
rows.anchor: ما عليك من عملهم ومن حساب عملهم من شيء

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The story resembles Noah's people calling his followers the lowly: the prophets defer their deeds and livelihood to God, and the poor believers' humble trades do not disgrace the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قال له قومه: {قالوا أنؤمن لك واتبعك الأرذلون}

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the repeated reckoning clause confirms parallel phrasing, though the second phrase could be omitted.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا المعنى أشار الزجاج

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: A second view concerns provision: neither the Prophet's nor the poor believers' livelihood depends on one another, because God provides for all; he should let them draw near.
rows.anchor: ليس رزقك عليهم ولا رزقهم عليك وإنما يرزقك وإياهم الله الرازق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The warning against becoming one of the wrongdoers means harming oneself through disobedience and losing reward; ظلم can mean diminution in Arabic and in Quranic usage.
rows.anchor: فتكون من الضارين لنفسك بالمعصية

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd calls expelling the poor injustice to them: they did not deserve it, so the author calls this a sound interpretation.
rows.anchor: إنهم لم يستحقوا منك الطرد فإذا طردتهم فقد ظلمتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weighing is on the day of questioning; al-wazn is the subject and al-haqq its predicate, and Ibn Abbas with most exegetes takes it as weighing people's deeds.
rows.anchor: على أن المراد بهذا الوزن أعمال العباد

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the scales establish the case against people, remove their excuses, and make God's justice clear.
rows.anchor: أكد الله به الاحتجاج على العباد وقطع به عذرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says God will set up a scale with a tongue and two pans to weigh people's good and evil deeds.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى ينصب ميزانا له لسان وكفتان يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says those made successful are saved, as in the verse about setting just scales on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: الناجون، قال: وهذا كما قال في سورة الأنبياء

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil calls the weighing justice and says a believer succeeds when even an atom's weight outweighs his sins.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: ({والوزن يومئذ الحق} وزن الأعمال يومئذ العدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source gives two accounts of how deeds are weighed: deeds assume beautiful or ugly forms, or the written records of deeds are weighed; the Prophet reportedly answered that records are weighed.
rows.anchor: أعمال المؤمن تتصور في صورة حسنة، وأعمال الكافر تتصور في صورة قبيحة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-Aʿmash interpret weighing and scales as justice and judgment, figurative expressions rather than literal weighing.
rows.anchor: كان مجاهد والضحاك والأعمش (¬6) يفسرون الوزن والميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet uses 'my scale for every disputant' to mean words equal to an opponent's; figuratively, scales can denote justice and records that accurately report deeds.
rows.anchor: قد كنت قبل لقائكم ذا مرة ... عندى لكل مخاصم ميزانه

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq says the figurative argument is linguistically valid, but authentic reports mentioning a scale should take precedence.
rows.anchor: أبو إسحاق: (وهذا كله في باب اللغة والاحتجاج سائغ

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari chooses literal weighing because reports converge, most scholars agree, and the Quran's surface supports it; the plural can reflect generic من or a plural referent.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول هو اختيارنا لتتابع الأخبار به واتفاق أكثر أهل العلم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another grammarian says mawāzīn means things weighed, not multiple scales; it refers to weighed deeds.
rows.anchor: الموازين هاهنا جمع موزون لا جمع ميزان

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies those with light scales as disbelievers.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: {ومن خفت موازينه}. قال مقاتل: (يعني: الكفار)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says a disbeliever's deeds appear in their ugliest form, weigh little, and lead him to the Fire; a believer whose good deeds are light is rescued by the testimony of God's oneness and Muhammad's messengership.
rows.anchor: يؤتى بعمل الكفار في أقبح سورة، فيوضع في كفة الميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further report says the Prophet produces a fingertip-sized card of the believer's blessings upon him; it outweighs his deeds, and the Prophet identifies it when the believer asks who he is.
rows.anchor: أخرج رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من حجزته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains losing oneself as arriving at punishment and wronging God's signs as rejecting what Muhammad brought.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: صاروا إلى العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajal is the appointed time that ends a period of respite.
rows.anchor: معنى الأجل: الوقت [المؤقت] (¬1) المضروب لانقضاء المهل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and Muqatil take the term here as the time for punishment: it cannot be delayed or brought forward once due; al-Hasan specifies annihilation, and Muqatil says it follows their demand for punishment.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: {ولكل أمة أجل} (يريد: وقتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the punishment deadline because the verse says every community has a term, rather than every individual.
rows.anchor: القول الأول أقوى لقوله: {ولكل أمة}، ولم يقل:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative is each person's lifespan; 'community' could describe the near-equal lifespans of people in each era as one shared term.
rows.anchor: لكل أحد إخبارا عن تقارب أعمار أهل كل عصر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says they are not delayed even by less than an hour; the hour is named because it is the smallest time-unit word.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: (ولا أقل من ساعة، ولكن ذكرت الساعة لأنها أقل أسماء الأوقات)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although advancing a deadline after it arrives seems impossible, Arabic can say winter has come when its onset approaches; thus they are not delayed after expiry or advanced as expiry nears.
rows.anchor: هذا على المقاربة؛ لأن العرب تقول: جاء الشتاء إذا قارب وقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'when their term comes' can cover both the end of the term and its approaching end.
rows.anchor: ولفظ قوله: {إذا جاء أجلهم} محتمل للمعنيين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One interpretation identifies the impure and pure as disbelievers and believers; the purpose clause attaches to the disbelievers' being gathered to Hell, separating the wretched from the blessed.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بالخبيث والطيب (¬2) في هذه الآية: الكافر والمؤمن، وهو قول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مرة الهمداني
rows.claim: Murra says God distinguishes believers, whom He created pure in prior knowledge, from disbelievers, whom He created impure; the impure are joined together for Hell.
rows.anchor: قال مرة: يميز المؤمن في علمه السابق

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth defines r-k-m as piling one thing over another until it forms a heap, like piled sand or clouds; exegetes say the impure are gathered into Hell like a mass of clouds.
rows.anchor: قال الليث: الركم: جمعك شيئا فوق شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular verb refers back to the singular khabīth, explaining the singular grammatical form.
rows.anchor: ووحد الخبر (¬4) لتوحيد قوله: {الخبيث}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ataa's report from Ibn Abbas says this community's judgment was deferred to the Last Day, unlike earlier nations; believers hidden in disbelievers' loins are then separated, as in 36:59.
rows.anchor: وروى عطاء عن ابن عباس للآية معنى آخر على هذا الطريق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: On this report, the impure are packed into Hell and constrained like a garment folded or beads threaded onto a string, with forelocks joined to feet, as in 69:32.
rows.anchor: مثل ما يدرج الثوب، يريد: {فيؤخذ بالنواصي والأقدام}

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes the pure and impure as believers' spending in jihad and disbelievers' expenditure against Muhammad; al-Kalbi says evil and good deeds are repaid with Hell and Paradise.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بالخبيث والطيب: نفقة الكافر على عداوة محمد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd calls spending for God's cause pure and spending in Satan's cause impure; the latter is cast into Hell and its owners told to join it.
rows.anchor: الإنفاق الطيب في سبيل الله من الإنفاق الخبيث في سبيل الشيطان

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq and Ibn al-Anbari choose the spending interpretation: God separates what believers spend in obedience from what polytheists spend in disobedience.
rows.anchor: ما أنفقه المؤمنون في طاعة الله مما أنفقه المشركون

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Asked why insentient wealth is thrown into Hell, Abu Bakr answers that God can make their unlawful wealth a means of pain, as in 9:35.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى يجعل أموالهم الحرام في النار ليعذبهم بها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj likewise says the wealth is piled in the fire and made to burn its owners, as the heated hoards brand them in 9:35.
rows.anchor: يجعل ما أنفقه المشركون بعضه على بعض ويجعل ذلك عليهم

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: A second answer is that Hell displays the worthlessness of wealth they prized and boasted of; a prophetic report depicts the adorned world asking to be given to a divine ally and being sent to the Fire as contemptible.
rows.anchor: ليري المؤثرين بها قلتها عنده وهوانها عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose clause li-yamīza attaches to the preceding statement that they will spend their wealth and then regret it.
rows.anchor: متعلقة بالكلام المتقدم {فسينفقونها ثم تكون عليهم حسرة}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The losers are the disbelievers who spent in Satan's service: their bargain failed because they bought afterlife punishment with their wealth.
rows.anchor: غبنت صفقتهم وخسرت تجارتهم أنهم اشتروا بأموالهم عذاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those reading yazīgh with ya match its masculine form to the preceding verb, making the two verbs parallel.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ (يزيغ) بالياء فوجهه تقدم الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated mention of God's repentance is not redundant: pardon comes first as grace before the sin is mentioned, then is repeated; it may also mean mercy upon mercy.
rows.anchor: كرر ذكر التوبة وهما واحد لأنه ليس في ابتداء الآية ذكر ذنبهم

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says God forgives a Muslim's sin twenty times; Ibn Abbas glosses 'then He turned to them' as increased approval.
rows.anchor: وقد قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three left behind are those deferred in 9:106, and the phrase means that God accepted their repentance; Ibn Abbas and Mujahid say they were held back from its acceptance.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء هم المعنيون بقوله: {وآخرون مرجون لأمر الله} الآية

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb ibn Malik, one of the three who stayed without excuse, says their absence was not the point: the Prophet had postponed deciding their case, as 9:106 says.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب بن مالك الشاعر -وكان أحد الثلاثة الذين تخلفوا بغير عذر-: (ما هذا من تخلفنا إنما هو تأخير رسول الله

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The earth felt constricted because believers would not speak or trade with the three, their wives were told to separate, and the Prophet turned away until their pardon after fifty days.
rows.anchor: المؤمنين منعوا من كلامهم ومعاملتهم، وأمر (¬2) أزواجهم باعتزالهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The constriction of their selves is distress in their hearts and loneliness when no believer spoke to them; they knew there was no refuge from God's punishment except with Him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد من الوحشة)

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: The order of the verse implies that recognizing their sin included an inward request for repentance; God accepted and showed mercy to that sincere intention before the text resumes with 'then He turned to them'.
rows.anchor: معرفة منهم بالذنب وإضمار للتوبة وطلب لها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The second mention of God's turning to them emphasizes increased approval and protection.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: ازداد لهم رضا وعصمة) (¬2)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's turning to them 'so that they might repent' means He gently enabled and guided them; without His will and enabling, a servant cannot repent.
rows.anchor: لطف لهم (¬3) في التوبة ووفقهم لها

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari also reads the phrase as God's turning so they persist in repentance or benefit from its reward; both depend on God's prior turning to them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: (معناه: ثم تاب عليهم ليدوموا على التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To detail the signs is to explain them; the people who know are those who infer God's power from indicators and proofs, unlike the ignorant.
rows.anchor: أي يتدلون بالأمارات والبراهين على قدرة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable compares the condition of worldly life to the described water, or means its quality is like water; worldly life here is the transient life of this world.
rows.anchor: وأراد بالحياة الدنيا الحياة الفانية في هذه الدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water makes the earth's plants intermingle: people eat vegetables, grains, and fruits, while livestock graze on pasture.
rows.anchor: فاختلط -بسبب ذلك الماء الذي أنزلناه- نبات الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the earth taking its adornment means its beauty and fertility; al-Zajjaj calls it complete beauty, while another view refers to the pleasing colors of flowers.
rows.anchor: يريد زينتها وحسنها وخصبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source links the word zukhru f to its earlier discussion in 6:112, where it occurs in 'adorned speech'.
rows.anchor: ومضى الكلام في معنى الزخرف عند قوله: {زخرف القول غرورا}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says 'adorned' refers to grain and fruit; another view refers to the plants themselves.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد بالحبوب

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives izzayyanat from tazayyanat by assimilating ta into zay and adding a joining alif; he compares 2:72 and 7:38.
rows.anchor: الزجاج: يعني: تزينت، فأدغمت التاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the land's people thought they could harvest, gather, and cut its crops; al-Zajjaj says they thought they could benefit from it.
rows.anchor: قادرون على حصادها وجدادها وقطعها

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Although the pronoun refers grammatically to the earth, the intended referent is its plants; another account takes it as the crop because context implies it.
rows.anchor: أخبر عن الأرض، والمعنى للنبات إذ كان مفهوما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God's command coming to the land means His punishment, that is, the command to destroy it.
rows.anchor: {أتاها أمرنا}، قال ابن عباس: يريد عذابنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains 'made it harvested' as leaving nothing there; al-Dahhak takes it as the harvested crop, while Abu Ubayda says completely uprooted and another view says cut or pulled out.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لا شيء فيها (¬2). وقال الضحاك

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth explains 'as if it had not flourished yesterday' as having vanished, from the verb for a people residing in their home; Ibn Abbas similarly says it was as if it had not existed.
rows.anchor: يقال للشيء إذا فني: كأن لم يغن بالأمس

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says it was as if the land had not been inhabited yesterday; Ibn Qutayba agrees, so this reading refers to the land rather than its produce.
rows.anchor: كأن لم تعمر بالأمس، والمغاني: المنازل التي يعمرها أهلها

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: A broader interpretation says it no longer stood in its former state, encompassing both the land and its produce; the discussion of 'yesterday' continues at 28:19.
rows.anchor: كأن لم تقم على تلك الصفة فيها قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as this parable has been explained, the Quran's signs are explained for people reflecting on resurrection.
rows.anchor: {كذلك نفصل الآيات} أي: كما بينا هذا المثل للحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The flourishing earth seems to promise enjoyment, then the one capable of destroying it returns it to nothing; worldly wealth and beauty likewise gather until death or disaster takes them away, warning against attachment and delusion.
rows.anchor: سلب ذلك عنه بموته أو بحادثة تأتي على ما قد جمعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ka-anna is the lightened form of the emphatic particle, with an omitted pronoun understood as ka-annahum; two poetic lines illustrate the construction.
rows.anchor: كأن) هذه هي المخففة من الثقيلة، التقدير: كأنهم لم يلبثوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the people seem to have stayed in their graves for only an hour of the day.
rows.anchor: كأن لم يلبثوا في قبورهم إلا قدر ساعة من النهار

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the interval between death and resurrection seems brief, as in 23:113.
rows.anchor: قرب عندهم ما بين موتهم وبعثهم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and Ibn al-Anbari say the time between death and resurrection feels like an hour because of the terror of resurrection and Judgment.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك وابن الأنباري: قصر عندهم مقدار الوقت الذي بين موتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes their brief stay as the duration of worldly life, not their time in the intermediate state.
rows.anchor: إنما قصرت عندهم مدة لبثهم في الدنيا لا مدة كونهم في البرزخ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, and Muqatil say people recognize each other when raised from their graves as they did in life, then recognition ends.
rows.anchor: يتعارفون بينهم حين بعثوا من القبور يعرف بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says recognition and awareness of who misled whom reproach them and establish proof against them.
rows.anchor: وفي معرفة بعضهم بعضا وعلم بعضهم بإضلال بعض التوبيخ لهم

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says their recognition is mutual accusation—'you led me astray'—not compassion; this fits 70:10 as a denial of merciful concern, while exegetes assign the two verses to different stages.
rows.anchor: فهذا تعارف توبيخ وتعنيف، وتباعد وتقاطع، لا تعارف عطف وإشفاق

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali offers two readings of yataʿārafūn: they discover how long they stayed, with the object omitted, or they recognize one another; the latter fits the exchanges in 37:50–51 and 52:26.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: معنى {يتعارفون} يحتمل أمرين؛ أحدهما: أن يكون المعنى يتعارفون مدة إماتتهم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali gives three syntactic parses for 'as though they had stayed': an adjective of the day with 'before it' omitted, an adjective of the verbal noun, or a circumstantial phrase attached to the object of 'We gather'.
rows.anchor: يحتمل قوله: {كأن لم يلبثوا} ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The second parse makes the phrase an adjective of the verbal noun 'gathering', with 'before it' omitted; the third makes it a state of the object, as if their condition were that of one who stayed only an hour.
rows.anchor: الوجه الثاني: أن تجعله صفة للمصدر على تقدير: ويوم نحشرهم حشرا

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Yawm may be governed by yataʿārafūn as a time adverb or metaphorically as an object, like 'thief of the night the people of the house'; alternatively it may be governed by the meaning of ka-an lam yalbathū.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن يكون معمول {يتعارفون}، وينتصب على وجهين

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali calls the last syntactic option weak: whichever parse is chosen, the adjective cannot govern its noun or an already annexed day without violating Arabic word order and attachment rules.
rows.anchor: غير أن هذا الوجه ضعيف؛ لأن قوله: {كأن لم يلبثوا} لا يخلو

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators say those who denied resurrection lost the reward of Paradise.
rows.anchor: خسر ثواب الجنة الذين كذبوا بالبعث

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari links their loss to the preceding recognition: after describing resurrection and the resurrected, the verse states the loss of its deniers.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر البعث وذكر ما يصير إليه أحوال المبعوثين

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq reads the statement as explaining, after establishing resurrection, that whoever denies it has lost.
rows.anchor: من الله عز وجل -بعد أن بين أمر البعث- أنه من كذب به فقد خسر

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr offers another reading: they are already lost during the mutual recognition, when repentance and reprieve are no longer possible.
rows.anchor: قد خسر الذين كذبوا بلقاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation of this verse is given under 7:34 and 7:188.
rows.anchor: مفسرة في آيتين من سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of crossing the sea is discussed in al-Aʿraf; ittibāʿ means pursuing the first party to catch up, as in 7:175.
rows.anchor: الإتباع طلب اللحاق بالأول واستقصاء هذا مذكور في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghyan means seeking superiority without right, while ʿadwan means wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: البغي: طلب الاستعلاء بغير حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With open hamza, the verb 'believe' ordinarily takes a preposition, which is omitted here so the anna-clause becomes its object or genitive; with kasra, an unspoken 'I said' is understood, and this reading highlights that the confession expresses faith.
rows.anchor: يصل بحرف الجر نحو: {يؤمنون بالغيب}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and all exegetes say Pharaoh's declaration was rejected because he professed faith only as punishment arrived; only Jonah's people were accepted at that stage, before death was visibly present.
rows.anchor: فلم يقبل الله إيمانه عند [نزول العذاب

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes say the angels confronted Pharaoh with 'Now?'—he had delayed repentance, chosen temporary life, and sought it only when the gate closed; they identify Gabriel as the speaker.
rows.anchor: والمفسرون على أن جبريل خاطب فرعون بهذا الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-āna is attached to an omitted predicate supplied by context, such as 'now you believe', 'believe', or 'repent'.
rows.anchor: والظرف متعلق بمحذوف تدل عليه الحال، تقديره: الآن آمنت

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: The author of al-Naẓm argues a drowning man could scarcely utter the full confession; the verse reports the certainty and remorse God knew in Pharaoh's heart as speech, like inward speech represented in 58:8 and 76:9.
rows.anchor: علم ما وقع في قلبه حينئذ من اليقين والندامة على ما فرط منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reports God's practice with earlier nations: He saved the messengers and those who believed with them from what He inflicted on unbelievers.
rows.anchor: هذا إخبار عما كان الله يفعل في الأمم الماضية من إنجاء الرسل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: 'Likewise' means God will save believers with Muhammad from His punishment, in a deliverance like that granted to earlier believers.
rows.anchor: مثل ذلك الإنجاء ننجي المؤمنين بمحمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من عذابي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and others say 'a duty upon Us' means God has declared this promise and does not break it; what He promises must come to pass.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس (¬1) وغيره (¬2)، ومعنى الوجوب هاهنا: أنه أخبر بذلك
